item.title: Leading French supermarket retailer faces up to €200 million hit from riots, looting
item.description: A leading French supermarket retailer, Carrefour, has warned that riots, looting and curfews across France could cost it between €80 million and €200 million in operating income, forcing it to cut its ...
item.content:encoded:
Leading French supermarket retailer faces up to €200 million hit from riots, looting A leading French supermarket retailer, Carrefour, has warned that riots, looting and curfews across France could cost it between €80 million and €200 million in operating income, forcing it to cut its annual earnings forecast amid disruptions to store operations, according to a Reuters report. ANI | Updated: 23-10-2026 17:42 IST | Created: 23-10-2026 17:42 IST

Visual from the protest in France (Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

A leading French supermarket retailer, Carrefour, has warned that riots, looting and curfews across France could cost it between €80 million (USD 90 million) and €200 million (USD 225 million) in operating income, forcing it to cut its annual earnings forecast amid disruptions to store operations, according to a Reuters report. The retailer has lowered its outlook for 2026 adjusted earnings per share (EPS) to stable or slight growth, compared with its earlier forecast of growth in the high single digits. It also expects free cash flow to decline slightly compared with 2025. According to Reuters, around 50 stores were attacked during the first day of unrest, with several looted and damaged. The company said the damage was considerable, while employees and business partners faced distressing situations. The unrest has disrupted trading at a critical time for the retail sector, as the fourth-quarter shopping period begins. Consumer confidence was already weak due to high fuel prices, and the ongoing disturbances have further affected customer footfall at stores. The retailer's finance chief said the direct costs included stolen or destroyed merchandise, damage to stores and equipment, and losses arising from outlets being forced to close. The company also expects continued disruption in the coming weeks, with some stores operating for shorter hours because of curfews. Reuters reported that many of the retailer's approximately 6,000 stores across France were closed in anticipation of further unrest, including on Sunday and Monday. The company did not disclose the total number of outlets shut. Costs have also risen as stores strengthened security arrangements, including hiring external security guards. The retailer was among those significantly affected because of its extensive network of convenience stores in major cities such as Paris, Lyon and Marseille. The company's chief executive called for improved security during the next round of planned protests on October 24, while acknowledging that further business disruption could not be ruled out. The impact of the unrest has also prompted the retailer to reduce its investment plans in France. It lowered its capital expenditure forecast for 2026 to €1.6 billion (USD 1.80 billion) from €1.7 billion (USD 1.91 billion). The company had been preparing to launch its Black Friday sales events in the coming days, adding to concerns over the timing of the disruption, Reuters reported. (ANI)

item.content:encoded:
China's Baidu tests robotaxi on London streets Reuters | Updated: 23-10-2026 17:30 IST | Created: 23-10-2026 17:30 IST

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

US-based Lyft unit Freenow and Baidu's Apollo Go unveiled the Chinese company's RT6 autonomous vehicle in London on Thursday and said they hope to launch a driverless robotaxi service in the city in 2027. The two companies began testing vehicles in London with safety drivers in the summer and hope to have fully driverless vehicles in the city next year, aiming for a commercial launch in 2027. The partnership between San Francisco-based ride-hailing firm Lyft and China's Baidu in London comes as the US Senate is working to pass a permanent ban on Chinese cars in the United States, pushing more companies to focus on Europe. Competition between robotaxi developers in London is heating up. UK self-driving vehicle startup Wayve and Lyft rival Uber launched a robotaxi service in London in September, initially with a human safety driver behind the wheel. US robotaxi company Waymo, a unit of Google parent Alphabet , aims to launch a fully driverless ride-hailing service in London by the end of this year. LONDON STREETS OFFER CHALLENGING TEST Freenow UK general manager Danny O'Gorman said London was a particularly good testing ground, with lots of speed bumps, narrow streets and many roads limited to 20 miles per hour. "So the car is going through the phase of learning the rules of the road much like you would do if you're trying to pass your own driving test," O'Gorman told Reuters during a demonstration ride. O'Gorman said the company was working closely with Transport for London and expected regulatory guidelines in the coming week. He recognised new technology "can sometimes be scary" but most Londoners were excited about the prospect He said robotaxis were not trying to replace London's famous black cabs. The firm is talking about "tens of vehicles in the next year or two" as it tests the market. "In terms of the taxi in London, the iconic black cab, this is not a replacement for that service," he said. "Black cabs are a fundamental part of London."

item.content:encoded:
India became third-largest exporter of arms to Europe: Defence Secretary RK Singh Defence Secretary said, our exports have reached an all-time high of 38,424 crores, which is about 3.6 billion euros, and I was reading a Bloomberg report yesterday, which said that suddenly over the last year, India became the third largest exporter of arms to Europe, mainly because of the Rearm Europe initiative. ANI | Updated: 23-10-2026 17:15 IST | Created: 23-10-2026 17:15 IST

Defence Secretary Rajesh Kumar Singh (Photo/ANI). Image Credit: ANI

Country:

India

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Defence Secretary Rajesh Kumar Singh on Friday asserted that India has rapidly emerged as the third-largest arms exporter to Europe, driven by surging demand under the "Rearm Europe" initiative and a broadening domestic manufacturing base. In the Agrasar Bharat Manch Event on Friday, Singh emphasised that in India, our intention is to build up our defence industrial base, which traditionally used to be focused on some 16 odd public sector companies, government-owned companies, to a much wider defence industrial base, including the private sector, the small and medium sector, as well as the startup ecosystem that is becoming very strong in India. Defence Secretary stated that the tangible economic and operational dividends of this transition are already materialising on a global scale. He said, "In India, on the other hand, for the last 10 years, we've seen tremendous growth in our defence ecosystem. We have some, besides the 16 large public sector companies. We now have almost 840 odd companies with industrial licenses that are large and medium-sized, and some 17,000 small and medium enterprises, including startups. And the result of this diversified industrial base is becoming visible in terms of the value of domestic sales, which are now almost 17 billion euros." Reflecting on recent trade reports, the Defence Secretary noted that international market dynamics have shifted drastically in India's favour over the past year. "Our exports have reached an all-time high of 38,424 crores, which is about 3.6 billion euros, and I was reading a Bloomberg report yesterday, which said that suddenly over the last year, India became the third largest exporter of arms to Europe, mainly because of the Rearm Europe initiative. As a result, a lot of standard ammunition of different types, artillery shells, and large- and small-calibre ammunition started getting exported to Europe in significant numbers," Singh stated. "We now export to more than 80 countries, and the in terms of policy, what we try to do is ensure that 75% of our capex every year, which is somewhere between 20 to 25 billion dollars every year, gets spent within the country, and we try to prioritise what we call IDDM, which is Indian-designed, developed and manufactured, to ensure technological sovereignty," he added. According to Secretary Singh, the nation's military exports have scaled to an all-time high, distributing defence products to more than 80 countries globally. Beyond heavy artillery and ammunition, Indian defence shipments range from tactical gear like helmets and bulletproof jackets to small arms. Emphasising that Indian defence shipments span a diverse spectrum of tactical goods and combat platforms, Singh said, "I mentioned that suddenly out the globe, we become the third largest whatever arms to Europe, one, mainly because of the artillery. In addition, we export a variety of equipment, including everything from bulletproof jackets and helmets to small arms.  A lot of buyers, particularly in Southeast Asia, have contracts that are all in public negotiations. So here's a whole gammate of different types of defence components. Small arms of different types, artillery, gun systems of different types." "These are the main platforms that we export to over 80 countries," he added. "We used to rely on Russia as its largest defence supplier. We still have a lot of our equipment that is of Russian origin, but over time that dependence has come down and we diversified; we already have fairly strong bilateral relations with some European countries, France in particular. But also with several other countries as well. After Russia, France has the largest share of defence Imports, about 15% or so, they and Israel are almost equal in defence.  I've just been on a visit to Greece and Cyprus, which are countries with whom we see a lot of strategic alignment. They are also recent partners; this is also our gateway," the Secretary stated. Singh emphasised that this diversification allows India to scale up production rapidly to meet international procurement demands. He said, "India intends to increasingly take part in Europe's arms procurement program. Not directly, but by setting up joint ventures in Europe. And of course, European Partners to set up joint ventures in India to access our defence market, and for us to set up joint ventures in Europe to access the European government programmes." "Foreign entities aiming to tap into India's domestic procurement programs will continue to face local manufacturing compliance mandates, though officials acknowledge structural similarities in regional offset frameworks. While European firms are welcome to tap into India's lucrative procurement pipelines, officials emphasised that foreign entities must strictly comply with local manufacturing benchmarks, noting structural parallels between regional regulatory frameworks," Defence Secretary added. Singh further stated that European countries can also take part in India's arms procurement programme, but they will have to meet our Make in India. He said, "European countries can also take part in India's arms procurement programme, but they will have to meet our Make in India. Now when we want to go to Europe, we understand that we have you have similar norms, except that yours are a bit lighter. I think it's 25% localisation. requirements is there as against a minimum 50% here, but the spirit of these programmes is similar. And I hope that this partnership agreement can lay the base for a situation where the supply chains between European and Indian defence manufacturers become increasingly integrated, and that is what we sort of intend to work on." (ANI)

item.title: Pakistan forces face allegations of abuse, cash seizure during Nushki operation
item.description: Residents of Nushki district in Balochistan have accused Pakistan’s Frontier Corps (FC) personnel of mistreating civilians during a security operation and withholding cash seized during their ...
item.content:encoded:
Pakistan forces face allegations of abuse, cash seizure during Nushki operation Residents of Nushki district in Balochistan have accused Pakistan’s Frontier Corps (FC) personnel of mistreating civilians during a security operation and withholding cash seized during their detention, as reported by The Balochistan Post. ANI | Updated: 23-10-2026 13:05 IST | Created: 23-10-2026 13:05 IST

Representative Image (File Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Residents of Nushki district in Balochistan have accused Pakistan’s Frontier Corps (FC) personnel of mistreating civilians during a security operation and withholding cash seized during their detention, as reported by The Balochistan Post. According to The Balochistan Post, several residents of Killi Faqiran were detained on suspicion following a shooting on the bypass road near the Deputy Commissioner’s residence two days earlier. The individuals were subsequently released after questioning. In a written complaint submitted to the Inspector General of FC Balochistan and the Corps Commander, the affected residents alleged that security personnel entered their homes, verbally abused them and instructed all men to assemble at a designated location. The complainants claimed that personnel confiscated their mobile phones, wallets and cash. They said they counted the money they were carrying before handing it over to the security personnel. The residents further alleged that their shirt hems were tied together before they were taken to FC headquarters and compelled to raise slogans during the journey. Although their phones and wallets were reportedly returned after their release, the cash allegedly remained missing. When they sought the return of their money, personnel allegedly dismissed their concerns. The complainants have urged the Corps Commander, the FC Inspector General and other senior officials to conduct an impartial investigation into the alleged mistreatment, damage to their homes and disappearance of their money. They have also demanded legal proceedings and departmental action against those found responsible. The residents stated that alleged high-handedness against ordinary citizens could further aggravate public resentment in Nushki, where security concerns and tensions remain significant, as highlighted by The Balochistan Post. The allegations come amid similar complaints from other parts of Balochistan. In September, residents of Kasano in Tump, Kech district, accused Pakistani forces of conducting house searches, taking valuables, physically abusing residents and setting fire to a house belonging to Ikram Baloch, as reported by The Balochistan Post. (ANI)
